articles.chapeau: Grand Theft Auto 6's day one sales reveals a mind-blowing statistic.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6's day one sales reveals a mind-blowing statistic.
Rockstar Games has revealed the pre-sales numbers that Grand Theft Auto VI generated prior to its November 19 launch.
Unsurprisingly, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI has become the biggest entertainment launch in history.
Rockstar's games have always sold exceedingly well, but combined with the 99 Metacritic score and 13 years of hype, the latest release has solidified itself as the most successful video game launch in history, and it'll probably never be topped by anything else.
As revealed by Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, Grand Theft Auto VI has sold 32.5 million units pre-release across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
In terms of total revenue this generated, sales are estimated to have hit $3.79 billion, which has already recuperated costs for the game. These numbers are based on company estimates through to the end of the day of November 19 th worldwide.
“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI ,” said Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser. “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”
Read More: Fanatical launches massive Black Friday sale with GTA 6, Resident Evil Requiem and more discounted
To put this into perspective, the number comes exceedingly close to the lifetime sales of the Nintendo 64, which has shifted 32.93 million units since 1996 according to the latest data from Nintendo.
It's also more than other consoles that were considered a success such as the Sega Mega Drive (30.75 million), the original Xbox (24 million), and the Nintendo GameCube (21.74 million).
In addition to that, GTA VI has already become the 30th best-selling game of all time in its first day alone.
For context, it took Elden Ring three years to hit the same number of sales. It's also beaten games like It Takes Two , Call of Duty Black Ops Cold War , and Super Mario Odyssey which were all resounding successes at the time they released.
Comparing this to other Rockstar games, GTA V sold around 11 million copies in the first day of release, while Red Dead Redemption 2 shifted 17 million copies within its first week. In total, GTA V has sold 235 million sales across its lifetime, coming in third place only behind Minecraft (425 million), and Tetris (520 million).
Meanwhile, Red Dead Redemption 2 is the fourth best-selling game of all time, with total lifetime copies sold reaching 89 million.
As for where other Grand Theft Auto games land on the list of best-selling video games, San Andreas sold 27.5 million copies across its lifetime, while Vice City sold 17.5 million units and GTA III sold 14.5 million units.
Analysts are confident that GTA VI will eventually beat GTA V as Rockstar Games' most successful game of all time, though this depends on the developer's implementation of Grand Theft Auto Online , which is where the bulk of the company's revenue comes from.
The game's online mode has been delayed, as it had with GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 before that, so that the company could focus on shipping the story mode.

Autodesk and Adobe are among those promising to make creating worlds and bringing ideas to life easier, often with little more than a prompt. Then I spent three weeks playing GTA 6, and it reminded me why I still find artists and designers so bloody impressive.
I've spent weeks exploring Rockstar's Leonida, and while GTA 6 is graphically stunning, it's the little things I keep coming back to. The shopfront branding, flyers that lead you to new characters, comic books on shelves, graffiti and fake adverts. Even Vice City's layout has a personality: all spaghetti junctions, back alleys and beachfront hotels, a world away from the calmer, goofier northern islands.
Rockstar has said it designs buildings by imagining who would live in them and how they'd spend their days. "For every visual design, we are getting into the heads of the people who would have inhabited that place and role-playing how the final look would have come about," says Miriam Bellard, Vice President of Art: Visual Development, in my interview with the studio. I love that approach. You aren't just making a building look convincing; you're thinking about the person who might have put that sofa there, chosen that colour or let the garden get overgrown.
The same thought goes into the animation , to the extent that Rockstar spent months perfecting how Lucia opens a door with her hip . I properly laughed out loud when a very large resident giggled, stumbled and tipped over a railing into a river. In one bar, a drunk woman trails Jason around, being annoying in exactly the way drunk people are. There's a sequence where you drunkenly try to find your hotel room, and it's the kind of disorientation many of us have felt, both with alcohol and with modern architecture where every corridor looks the same. Out in the woods, two deer nuzzle each other. These little moments don't advance the plot, but they're the sort of thing that makes me want to keep exploring.
The weather is another thing I've found myself stopping to look at, from morning sun cutting through mist over wildflower meadows to storm clouds swallowing the skyline. Rain changes what you can see and hear, and flying a plane through a storm is shaky, stubborn and hard . In a nightclub, smoke and reflected light leave you disoriented, just as they should. In fact, Rockstar has spent years hiding GTA 6's environmental storytelling in details you might never notice. There's an awful lot of work behind getting these moments right, and you can feel it when you're playing.
I've also been surprised by how much I care about Jason and Lucia, and how much of that comes down to the game's art, design and animation. I caught myself shooting enemies in the arms and legs instead of finishing them off because I wanted Lucia to think well of Jason, and because it gets too grim to kill people in a game that looks this realistic. It's an odd thing to admit about GTA, but I started feeling uncomfortable with some of the violence. The writing, animation, and character design had me invested in two people who don't exist in a world built in polygons.
There's a lot of noise about AI generating images, making environments and producing assets faster , and I can see the appeal, but creativity goes well beyond making something that looks good. It's the decisions about what goes into a scene, what gets left out, how a character reacts, when a joke lands and how some seemingly insignificant detail can make someone feel something. articles.t: GTA 6 Glitch Unlocks The FPS On Xbox Series X|S, But With Multiple Drawbacks
articles.chapeau: It
articles.txt:
If there's anything we could add to GTA 6 as things stand, it'd be an official 60FPS mode. That's obviously not possible right now due to how demanding the game is on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S hardware, even in the case of the PS5 Pro.
Interestingly though, over the weekend, players have discovered the ability to activate what some are calling a "60FPS Glitch" or "60FPS Bug" on Xbox consoles, forcing the game to unlock its FPS and run at a higher frame rate than it's actually supposed to.
Someone called Meowwie64 on Reddit appears to have found this, and here's what they did to activate it:
Now, as mentioned, there are multiple drawbacks here. The first one is that the glitch speeds up most aspects of the game, making it run faster than intended (and look like it's in fast-forward mode!). This is obviously not an ideal way to enjoy GTA 6, and serves as an immediate deal-breaker in my view.
Another one is that reaching 60FPS is pretty much impossible under normal gameplay circumstances. If you're driving down a highway, for example, you're likely only going to get around 35-40FPS at max, with 60FPS and above being saved for situations that require no graphical intensity whatsoever.
And finally, it should be noted that GTA 6 was never intended to be run this way on Xbox Series X|S, and therefore you could run into all sorts of issues - crashes, bugs, maybe even your console overheating. That last one is unlikely, but the game has been specifically built to run at 30FPS on these machines, so it's not worth pushing it in our view.

GTA 6 Makes It Nearly Impossible to Play Without Killing Anyone
articles.chapeau: Turns out trying not to kill anyone in Grand Theft Auto 6 is as difficult as you’d expect
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is out now, and for my initial playthrough of Rockstar’s latest giant open-world game, I wanted to try something a bit out of left field: How long could I play without killing anyone? I’d do my best Batman impression: brutally beating my foes, crippling them with excessive medical debt, but keeping them alive.
Yeah, that didn’t last long. Turns out trying to not commit crime in the game that’s all about committing crime is a difficult task.
The first mission was easy enough. Jason has to rescue drug runner Donnie from a gang of rednecks who keep tigers in cages. (Surely that will end well for them.) After I rescued him, I got into a fist fight with a beefy boy and knocked him out. So far so good. Jason had a pistol on him and could pick up weapons around the swamp base, but, trying to avoid a shootout at all costs, I stealthily booked it away from the rednecks and toward the water, avoiding any detection (and potential for violence).
That was the opening mostly-on-the-rails mission, but things quickly went south when I was left to my own devices. During the next in-game day, players are given a few mission options. I met up with Cal, Jason’s buddy who’s not cut out for a life of crime, and we drove to a police impound lot. I needed to steal a car with a trunk full of weed, and this is where shit hit the fan.
Look, I never learned how to drive in real life, and am not the biggest fan of it in video games. Driving for more than a few feet without hitting anything or anyone is an impossible challenge in games, and driving in GTA 6 feels especially difficult; I can never figure out the right speed to go, and sharp turns are the bane of my existence.
So maybe I was always doomed to run over a cop on my way out of the impound lot.
Image: Rockstar Games via Polygon Police officers swarmed Jason after he unhooked the red Phoenix and hotwired it. Too much was happening at once: an on-screen message about how I could open the gate, cops flinging open the driver’s side door and trying to rip Jason from the vehicle, and police radio chatter pouring out of my controller speaker. I’m not ashamed to say I restarted this mission several times just trying to figure out how to get out of the lot by carefully not running over any cops.
And then, who pulls up in front of the gate I’m about to crash through but a do-gooder cop hopping out of his vehicle? I assumed the giant pool of blood leaking out of him after our collision meant he wasn’t long for the world.
I did get caught on that attempt (again, driving is hard), and had to restart. On my next attempt, I got away blood free. Did that mean I succeeded in not killing anyone, or did the roadkill cop mean I failed? Didn’t matter, since soon after I killed someone and there was no going back.
After purchasing a longarm from an Ammu-Nation, Jason gets jumped. This was my first fistfight, meaning I had to navigate on-screen messages telling me how to fight while trying not to die. I was just pressing buttons, y’all. Instinctively I pressed whatever button flashed up on screen, which meant, after knocking out one dude, I picked up his knife and started attacking with it. Knives — much more lethal than Jason’s fists!
I killed one goon before dropping the knife and knocking out the third and final guy. I checked my playthrough stats and, yep, that guy was definitely dead. And I was barely two hours into the game. There’s a lot to do in GTA 6 , and plenty of control schemes to learn just to be able to do all that stuff . Players have already accidentally kicked bodega cats (heinous) because of a fumbled button press.
Image: Rockstar Games Still, not to be deterred by my early-game kills, I tried to soldier on with committing as little murder as possible. I soon learned this was impossible. During the “Hey, Arnold” mission, Jason gets into a car chase with one of landlord Brian’s old buddies. Arnold’s got goons on motorcycles protecting him and, ya know, I said I wasn’t very good at driving.
I tried my damndest not to kill them, but that wasn’t going to happen. I accidentally ran into some, and they didn’t survive their facetime with Brian’s big-ass truck. But, hey, at least I got to spare Arnold at the end.
I’ve played a few hours since, and have tried to keep up my “no killing” policy. It’s especially tough in shootouts as Rockstar’s third-person shooting has never been the most fluid, and aiming for nonvital parts of people — when getting shot at myself — is a tall task.

Cyberleek Claims to Release 209 GB GTA VI Xbox Build
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek claims to have released a 209 GB Xbox build of GTA VI without its executable and threatens to publish the missing file on November 23.
articles.txt:
19 Reads Last Update Nov 22, 2026 - 19:29 Share WhatsApp Smallest Font Largest Font A hacker operating under the name Cyberleek claims to have obtained and distributed a 209 GB Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI, raising the possibility that PC modders could eventually run the game through emulation before Rockstar Games releases an official PC version. The claim appeared on Cyberleek's website on November 21, 2026.
According to Cyberleek, the files represent the full November 2026 build of the game. However, the download reportedly excludes the executable file required to run the software, meaning the leaked files cannot currently launch as a playable game.
Cyberleek announced the alleged release through a statement on its website: "It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent."
Reddit users have subsequently shared files they claim contain assets from the leaked build. Cyberleek has also threatened to publish the missing executable on November 23.
The hacker described the conditions surrounding the planned release, linking its timing to a cryptocurrency market valuation. Cyberleek stated: "The countdown is the timer for the final file. Zero, and the executable drops, no conditions. Unless the CYBERLEEK token reaches 15 million market cap first — then it drops immediately."
Cyberleek's previous activities have included releasing early Grand Theft Auto VI footage and publishing a manifesto called the CYBERLEEK Edict. The manifesto promoted consumer rights, while the hacker also launched a cryptocurrency under the name $CYBERLEEK before disappearing from public view.
Take-Two Interactive has previously attempted to identify the person or people behind the Cyberleek identity. Despite those efforts, the individual or group has continued making claims involving the unreleased game.
Cyberleek argues that the Xbox build could provide an opportunity for PC modders to run Grand Theft Auto VI through emulation. Although the game is available on Xbox, an official PC port has not been released.
In explaining the alleged potential for emulation, Cyberleek claimed: "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons."
The claim suggests that modding communities could attempt to make the game playable on PC using the leaked Xbox files. However, the absence of the executable remains a significant limitation, and Cyberleek's promised November 23 release has not yet been confirmed.

articles.txt:
If you’re looking for one of the fastest cars in GTA 6, the Piccia Furia, then you’ve come to the right place. The chances are, you’re looking for this supercar for Randy’s wishlist, and to be honest, it’s quite easy to get to.
If you’re still completing Randy’s wishlist and looking for more cars, we recommend checking out our master hub after this article for all the car locations .
But without keeping you waiting any longer, let’s jump into where you can find the Piccia Furia.
The Piccia Furia location may appear on your map if you call Randy when you’re halfway through his list.
To find the Piccia Furia, head to Peacock Estates , just to the right of the writing on your map that says ‘South Vice-Dale County’.
Here, there’ll be a mansion that is guarded by some security guards walking around; you can either choose to take them out, or simply hop over the hedges to the left
Once you’re inside the front garden, go to the garage on the left and open the door. Here you’ll see the Piccia Furia in blue. From here, it’s relatively straightforward: clone the key, smash through the gates, and make your getaway.
As always, fix your car at the gas station near Randy’s garage before taking it to him. The gas station is within Randy’s tracker blocker range, so you don’t need to worry about stopping the car. Once you give the Piccia Furia to Randy in perfect condition, he will give you a massive $10,000 bonus, so it’s worth taking the time and spending $ 1,000-$ 2,000 to fix the car if it needs it.

articles.t: Leonida Brings GTA 6 PC Porting Tools to GitHub
articles.chapeau: The open-source Leonida project helps convert GTA 6 Xbox assets and shaders for PC, but the game cannot launch without a completed executable loader.
articles.txt:
203 Reads Last Update Nov 22, 2026 - 18:48 Share WhatsApp Smallest Font Largest Font PC developers have gained a new set of tools for working with the Xbox Series X version of Grand Theft Auto VI following the appearance of Leonida on GitHub on November 22, 2026. The open-source project aims to transform the console version into a native Windows application by translating system calls and graphics instructions into formats compatible with PC hardware.
According to the project's documentation, Leonida uses static recompilation to translate the console environment into a PC-compatible implementation. Its graphics conversion process transforms compiled RDNA2 programs into SPIR-V, allowing them to work through the Vulkan graphics API.
The project is distributed under the GPL-3.0 license. Its developers state that the repository does not include copyrighted game files, encryption keys, or executable modules.
Despite its progress, Leonida cannot currently launch Grand Theft Auto VI. The developers still need an executable file to complete the loader and the D3D12 graphics layer required for the Vulkan implementation.
However, the existing tools already demonstrate several working resource-conversion capabilities. According to the project information, Leonida can extract and convert all 26 game shaders into SPIR-V format.
The toolkit also supports exporting 3D models into OBJ files, textures into DDS format, and audio tracks into Ogg Opus or WAV files. These functions allow developers to examine and process different game assets without having a functioning PC version.
Building the project requires an unpacked Xbox Series X copy of Grand Theft Auto VI version 1.0.2.1 with readable files. The automated utilities locate the game installation and extract the necessary resources before generating shaders locally.
Windows 10 or Windows 11 in a 64-bit configuration is required for the main development environment. Users also need approximately 350 GB of available disk space to accommodate the working files.
The software requirements include Python 3.12 or later, .NET 8 SDK, Vulkan SDK, and LLVM 21 or later with AMD architecture support. Developers must also install Visual Studio 2022 with its C++ desktop components, Windows SDK version 10.0.26100 or later, and FFmpeg for audio conversion.
Linux users can also perform resource extraction and shader validation, according to the project documentation. The executable loader is intended to run through compatibility platforms such as Wine or Proton once the necessary components become available.
The project's development community has also expanded, with its GitHub repository attracting more than 8,200 stars and 147 contributors. Ongoing development includes improvements to graphics-command translation and support for emulating 64-thread shader groups on NVIDIA and Intel graphics cards.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leaker Ties PC Build Release to Crypto Token Target
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek withholds a key executable until its crypto token reaches a $15 million market cap, despite promising a November 23 release.
articles.txt:
6 Reads Last Update Nov 22, 2026 - 17:54 Share WhatsApp Grand Theft Auto 6. Image: Rockstar Games/Decrypt Smallest Font Largest Font A leaked version of Grand Theft Auto 6 could reach PC users before Rockstar Games releases an official port, but a hacker known as Cyberleek is making the release of a crucial game file conditional on a cryptocurrency target. The developer of the leak has also promised to publish the file on November 23, 2026, regardless of whether the target is reached. According to PC Gamer, Cyberleek has distributed what it describes as a nearly complete 209 GB Xbox build of GTA 6 from November 2026 through a torrent.
However, the main executable remains unavailable, preventing modders from immediately attempting to run the game on PC. The executable is the missing component Cyberleek says could enable work on emulating the leaked Xbox version on PC. Its release is tied to the market capitalization of a cryptocurrency token called CYBERLEEK.
Cyberleek has set a $15 million market capitalization target for an early release. That figure represents half of the $30 million target previously proposed by the leaker in October.
As of the weekend, CYBERLEEK was trading at approximately $0.002, with a market capitalization of around $1.3 million. According to the reported figures, the token remained more than $13 million below the requested threshold. The token had also declined approximately 20% over the week. However, its limited liquidity means that market prices and capitalization figures could fluctuate substantially.
The arrangement has prompted concerns among cryptocurrency observers about the possibility of a speculative price increase followed by a rug pull, a practice in which token promoters abandon a project after attracting buyers. Cyberleek has separately claimed to possess a PlayStation 5 build that could serve as an alternative if the Xbox files prove unusable. Neither the claimed Xbox version nor the PlayStation 5 files have been independently verified as genuine.
The incident highlights the growing overlap between cryptocurrency speculation, game piracy, and artificial intelligence-assisted development. Modern Xbox game architecture is considered closer to conventional PC software than PlayStation architecture, potentially making certain emulation and porting efforts more accessible. AI coding tools have also accelerated decompilation work, contributing to a broader wave of AI-assisted game porting projects during 2026.
These developments have increased attention on the technical possibilities surrounding unofficial PC versions of console games. GTA 6 has also been associated with other cryptocurrency-related speculation. A trader previously made approximately $66,000 from a GTA 6-themed meme coin amid confusion surrounding cryptocurrency ticker symbols.
Separately, the game's digital-only, disc-free release has fueled debate about consumer rights. GameStop's CEO has argued that digital-only games have negatively affected consumers.
Rockstar Games has not announced an official PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6. The company could also pursue legal action against unauthorized distribution of its intellectual property, while Cyberleek's promised executable release remains scheduled for November 23, 2026.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' on Xbox Series S: How well it runs
articles.chapeau: Here's the verdict.
articles.txt:
Reading through Reddit, there is no shortage of concerns about how well Xbox Series S will or won’t run the game. As the release neared, fans seemed confident that Rockstar Games would ensure the game was playable, but opinions varied widely on what graphical sacrifices would be required for it to run, including reduced crowd density and scaled-back visuals.
How much time did I spend sweating the idea of crowd density? Too much. Did I ever think about it or care about it until Redditors said it’ll likely be less on the Series S? Not at all.
And yet, while it filled me with regret for not buying a PS5 last Black Friday before the price hikes arrived, it did not stop me from buying GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, debating whether or not to resist the pull off the New Zealand timezone trick to play it early, and preparing to explore Leonida.
And now, having played GTA 6 for a few hours, I can tell you everything you need to know about how it runs and how it feels.
I won’t keep you waiting: GTA 6 runs smooth as butter on Xbox Series S. There were no stutters, no lag or other slowdowns that pulled me out of the gameplay.
During a prologue that introduced me to protagonists Jason and Lucia, I quickly experienced a variety of locations in daytime and nighttime, as well as rainy weather. After that, I was able to play around Leonida and check out all the basic things that might catch your attention as you play: how the weather looks, flying down the road in a car through busy streets, random tasks around Jason's home.
In addition to moving quickly through various areas, I also took a moment to slow down. I watched a sunset by the water, went for a swim surrounded by fish, and observed how the environment affected Jason. Nothing slowed down, glitched out, or made me think anything other than I was playing a AAA game.
What I can’t tell you right now is how much better GTA 6 is or isn’t on PS5 or any of the higher-end consoles. We’re in the process of comparing the Xbox Series S version to the PS5 Pro version as we speak.
Rockstar has explicitly said the game will run best on PS5 consoles, with faster load times and technology that may improve resolution. The PS5 Pro version will also include ray tracing, making the lighting even more eye-catching. But both games will still be locked at 30 frames per second, according to Rockstar. The game developer did not say if any other sacrifices had to be made to get it to run on the Xbox Series S.
Regardless, what I can tell you is there is a good game waiting for you to play on Xbox Series S. If you don’t have the funds to upgrade your console, do not let comparison be the thief of joy.
GTA 6 is a generational moment in gaming and a cultural moment much larger than any game launch I’ve ever seen. The game is fun, the music is a vibe, and the world is immersive without feeling like a chore. I can't imagine waiting to play this if they have the means to do so right now.

Cyberleek says it will hand over the executable on November 23, 2026, which is tomorrow, and claims the game could be “emulated inside a week.” Every one of those claims remains unconfirmed. Our earlier piece on the 209 GB Xbox dump and the missing emulator covered the first hours of the story. This analysis goes further and asks what a quick PC port would actually demand.
We separate what outlets have confirmed from what the leak source merely says, explain why one missing file changes everything, compare the realistic routes to a PC version, and close with five predictions. Cyberleek describes the distribution as a torrent, and the group’s own wording says so directly. That matters for a practical reason. A torrent spreads quickly and cannot be recalled, so whatever the archive contains is now in many hands. It also means the files reach people who have no way to check them against a trusted original.

articles.t: GTA 6 PS5 and Xbox users protest after bans for sharing gameplay with nudity
articles.chapeau: Microsoft and Sony are cracking down on lewd GTA 6 gameplay captured by players. Xbox and PS5 gamers received suspensions for uploading clips featuring sunbathing or nude NPCs. Some critics think that sharing unedited footage from the approved Rockstar title should be safe.
articles.txt:
Rockstar 's new title carries a mature age rating for violence, strong language, and occasional nudity . Players are discovering the risks of sharing GTA 6 gameplay clips with adult-oriented content. An Xbox user received a 48-hour suspension for an upload depicting scantily-clad beachgoers . Meanwhile, a PS5 gamer suffered a longer punishment after taking a photo of a nudist colony.
By default, the Xbox Network automatically shares captured in-game footage with friends. Redditor sangobar documented how a beach clip triggered a flag, resulting in a two-day suspension. An email claimed that the media violated Community Standards or the Microsoft Services Agreement. Although the poster couldn't appeal, the ban didn’t prevent access to the single-player campaign .
Sangobar argues the video contained no nudity and the discipline was unjust. GTA 6 PS5 players are also finding the guidelines for promoting mature gameplay unclear. On social media, DerrickGott007 says he was given a one-month restriction on PSN social features . In this instance, NPCs wearing no clothing were the culprit.
Fans first learned the Leonida map included nudist colonies in a Cyberleek video from a development build. DerrickGott007 snapped an in-game photo in one of these locations before sending it to an acquaintance. The messaging system flagged the inappropriate imagery and responded accordingly.
It’s unclear if a Microsoft or Sony employee reviewed the footage, but both companies rely on AI-powered monitoring . Particularly with the beach example, a human may have recognized there was no infraction. A 2025 Digital Safety Content Report from Microsoft disclosed a high rate of successful appeals for false positives.
Some gamers believe it shouldn’t be their responsibility to filter out adult content. Xbox and PlayStation approved the GTA 6 release for their consoles, aware of its mature age rating. At worst, they should block the distribution of offensive media without penalizing a user.
Series X and S owners can reduce their chances of a ban by turning off automatic uploads. Until Sony comments, PS5 fans should be cautious about what GTA 6 gameplay they record and share on PSN messaging.

Sign in to your XDA account Summary NotRexed is part of the team building Leonida, a project that aims to run the Xbox version of GTA 6 on PC. Leonida translates RDNA GPU code to SPIR-V and reads game assets from dumped Xbox images, but it currently lacks GTA 6 's executable. Cyberleek's leaked Xbox build of GTA 6, which comes in at 209GB, seems to be real. NotRexed , a key developer behind Hookshot , one of the first projects to bring the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time to PC through static recompilation, says they're now working on an unofficial PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 (the project was first announced on their Discord ). Leonida seems to be built around the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 , which recently appeared online courtesy of Cyberleek , the same person or team behind major leaks surrounding the game from earlier this year.
According to Leonida's description, since the Xbox Series X/S CPU is x86-64 like a PC, the "game's code is loaded and run[s} natively." The team behind the project, which includes assistance from Claude and roughly 75 other contributors, claims that the console's system software has also already been reimplemented.
Additionally, the Xbox Series X/S's "precompiled RDNA GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan" and the GTA 6 "models, textures, and audio" are all read directly from the disc image, which users need to provide from their own dumped copy of the Xbox version of GTA 6.
Like similar porting projects, Leonida doesn't feature GTA 6 's game files or keys. Right now, the game doesn't even boot on PC because the project is missing the game's executable, which Cyberleek's recent leak of the Xbox version doesn't include.
Credit: Rockstar Users on Reddit report that Cyberleek's Xbox build of GTA 6 features roughly 209GB of data. Screenshots of the leaked directory structure are also circulating online (check one out below). I haven't verified that the torrent is available (it's likely being shared through private trackers). Cyberleek says they'll release the missing executable file once a countdown expires, but that they'll drop it early if their shady cryptocurrency reaches $15 million in market capitalization (because, of course, a cryptocurrency scam is connected to this).
It's unclear how long it will take to get GTA 6 running on PC, but if the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is any indication, it could arrive sooner than expected. While GTA 6 is now available on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version. Rumors point to an official PC release arriving somewhere between six months and a year from now, similar to GTA V .
Hookshot was briefly pulled from GitHub after a dispute between NotRexed and the rest of the team behind the project. It's back on GitHub now, though. MagicBean's Longshot , a fork of Hookshot, continues the original project, with most of the team shifting over. In other GTA 6 -related news, with PS5 Remote Play or a capture card, plus apps like Veyra and a powerful gaming PC, several people have been able to run GTA 6 at 60fps and above with DLSS5 .

articles.txt:
Bluffton, OH From movies and tv to the lastest fashion trends and lifestyles. We are your one-stop for everything.
Remember Cyberleek? The Grand Theft Auto VI leaker with a meme coin and a dream claims to have dumped nearly the entire Xbox build of the game on launch day, and says the last missing piece is coming soon. It’s déjà vu, because we’ve been through this song and dance before.
On Oct. 10, Cyberleek tied a full build release to their coin’s market value hitting $30 million. The coin never came close and flamed out within days. This isn’t the first time it has crashed, either: Tom’s Hardware reported that the leaker cashed out roughly $250,000, mostly from accumulated trading fees, in late August, hours before Rockstar’s official gameplay reveal and just before the coin plunged.
That’s a bit like a magician announcing the big reveal and slipping out through the kitchen with the cash register. And what did we get in the meantime? Some Lucia clips picked by a fan poll and requested by basically nobody else, delivered with the energy of a guy who found a loophole in the “no refunds” policy.
Now the target has dropped to $15 million. Cyberleek says the final file is coming Monday, Nov. 23, no matter what, or sooner if the coin hits $15 million first. Half price, like a clearance rack at a Blockbuster that somehow survived into 2026 (OK, one of them did). Nothing says confidence like cutting your own ransom note in half and hoping nobody notices.
According to PC Gamer , Cyberleek says every file has been released except the main executable, from what the leaker calls the “full November 2026 build” of the game. Reports put the download at roughly 200 GB, with several outlets citing 209 GB. If that’s accurate, they’ve handed over the whole pantry and kept the oven. It’s like mailing someone every ingredient for a birthday cake, then standing outside their house holding the matches and asking for a tip.
One important caveat: as of this writing, nobody has confirmed the build is genuine. Everything about the build itself is Cyberleek’s claim. And files claiming to be Cyberleek builds have been linked to malware before, so this isn’t the torrent to get curious about.
Cyberleek’s pitch is that “this community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps.” Fine. Honestly, kind of compelling. I’ve watched grown adults argue about frame rates in a Walmart parking lot, so I understand the stakes. The catch: no working Xbox Series X emulator exists yet, according to Notebookcheck, so “inside a week” is doing a lot of heavy lifting.
GTA 6 has no official PC version, so Cyberleek is pitching emulation of the leaked console build as the way in. And if the Xbox build can’t be made to work, they say they’ll go after a PlayStation 5 build instead, a fallback they call “most likely never required.” Because apparently one console isn’t enough.
According to launch-day reports from PC Gamer and IGN, the meme coin was sitting at roughly $1.8 million to $1.9 million. Reaching $15 million in a few days would take an eightfold jump, the kind of growth you normally only see in a sourdough starter during lockdown, and even those eventually die in the back of the fridge. So the date is the trigger that actually matters: Monday, Nov. 23.
Maybe Cyberleek has the goods. Maybe they have a folder of loading screens and a very vivid imagination. Nobody knows, and my money’s on the second one, but if the build is real, Rockstar has a headache. Either way, we’ll find out soon. Grab some popcorn, and maybe a sturdy lawn chair.

articles.txt:
À peine sorti sur PS5 et Xbox, GTA 6 agite déjà la scène PC : le hacker Cyberleek promet un port jouable en une semaine grâce à une fuite Xbox. Entre build incomplète, memecoin et pression sur Rockstar, cette promesse intrigue autant qu’elle inquiète.
Depuis la sortie de GTA 6 le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, beaucoup se demandent encore quand la version PC arrivera. Un pirate qui se fait appeler Cyberleek promet d’abréger l’attente en rendant GTA 6 PC jouable en « moins d’une semaine » grâce à une fuite Xbox.
Dans un message du 19 novembre relayé par PC Gamer, le hacker affirme : « CL détient la build complète de novembre 2026 de Grand Theft Auto VI, et elle part en torrent, maintenant ». Il décrit une build de développement Xbox d’environ 209 Go et annonce un compte à rebours jusqu’au 23 novembre pour lâcher le fichier clé.
Selon les premiers retours de la scène sécurité comme VX‑Underground , les fichiers ressemblent à de vrais assets de Grand Theft Auto VI : textures, sons, scripts, données du moteur. Mais l’archive Xbox serait privée de son exécutable principal, le fameux .exe qui sert de chef d’orchestre. Sans lui, ces 209 Go restent un puzzle impossible à lancer.
C’est ce fichier que Cyberleek promet de publier, en expliquant qu’il s’agit « d’une build Xbox, pas d’une build PC » mais que « cette communauté l’aura émulée en moins d’une semaine, au‑delà de 30 fps ». Pour l’instant, rien ne prouve que l’exécutable soit réellement en sa possession.
Derrière la promesse de GTA 6 PC rapide se cache aussi un objectif financier. Le pirate lie la mise en ligne anticipée de l’exécutable au succès de son jeton crypto $CYBERLEEK : il réclame 15 millions de dollars, soit environ 14 millions d’euros de capitalisation, après un premier seuil à 30 millions de dollars, près de 28 millions d’euros, jamais atteint.
Sur le plan technique, cette promesse fait tiquer les spécialistes. Aucun émulateur Xbox Series X|S public ne sait aujourd’hui lancer un jeu aussi lourd que GTA 6 . Même avec le kit Xbox GDK , proche de Windows, il faudrait soit émuler tout l’environnement console, soit recompiler le code vers un exécutable PC, ce qui demande d’ordinaire des mois de travail.
Cette agitation attire déjà de faux sites « GTA 6 PC gratuit » et des launchers piégés par des malwares. Télécharger ces builds reste illégal en France, avec à la clé risques de poursuites et de vol de données.
Officiellement, Rockstar Games n’a toujours pas annoncé de version PC de Grand Theft Auto VI , même si des rumeurs évoquent un lancement début 2027 . L’ancien directeur technique Obbe Vermeij estime qu’un portage PC plus rapide serait dans l’intérêt du studio pour couper l’herbe sous le pied des ports sauvages dopés aux outils automatisés et des hackers comme Cyberleek .
En attendant une annonce officielle, la seule manière légale de profiter de GTA 6 sur un écran d’ordinateur reste le streaming de sa version PS5 ou Xbox via Remote Play ou Xbox Cloud Gaming. Entre menaces de leak, chantage au memecoin et protection juridique agressive de Rockstar, la promesse d’un GTA 6 PC jouable en une semaine tient plus du pari risqué que d’une feuille de route crédible.

Add preferred source An anonymous leaker known as Cyberleek has distributed a roughly 209 GB Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto 6 by torrent while withholding the main executable needed to attempt a PC port. The file is promised for Nov. 23, but would be released early if the CYBERLEEK meme coin reaches a $15 million market cap - down from an earlier $30 million target. The token was trading near $0.002 at a value of about $1.3 million, far short of the goal, and has drawn accusations of a pump-and-dump scheme. None of the files has been verified, Rockstar has announced no PC version, and security researchers report thousands of malware detections tied to fake GTA 6 downloads. Key Elements Cyberleek GTA 6 Rockstar Games CYBERLEEK token Grand Theft Auto PC Gamer Kaspersky GameStop PlayStation 5 Xbox A figure using the handle Cyberleek has posted what is described as a roughly 209 GB Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto 6 to torrent networks, but is holding back the one file that matters most to anyone hoping to run the game on a computer: the main executable.
According to PC Gamer, the leaker has attached a financial condition to that final piece. Cyberleek says the executable will be published on Nov. 23 either way, but will be released early if the CYBERLEEK meme coin reaches a $15 million market capitalization - half the $30 million threshold floated in October.
The market has not cooperated. The token was changing hands near $0.002 over the weekend, putting its value at roughly $1.3 million, or more than $13 million below the stated trigger. It has shed about 20% over the past week, though pricing on a micro-cap asset with very little liquidity can swing violently in either direction.
The missing executable is the piece that would allow modders to begin the work of recompilation - adapting console code so it runs on PC hardware - potentially delivering a playable version long before Rockstar Games plans to sell one. The leaker has said the process could take about a week once the file is available, and has also claimed to hold a PlayStation 5 build as a fallback should the Xbox files prove unusable.
None of the leaked material has been independently verified as authentic, and Rockstar has announced no PC version of the game. The publisher, which has a long record of litigating against leaks and cheats, could pursue legal action rather than tolerate a port.
Skepticism has been loud. Critics have described the arrangement as a shakedown or, worse, an attempt to inflate the coin ahead of a rug pull - the crypto maneuver in which a token's backers abandon it after attracting buyers.
Note: Market figures reflect thin trading in a small-cap token and can change sharply.
The episode lands at the intersection of three trends that have been converging all year: crypto speculation, game piracy and AI-assisted coding. Modern Xbox titles are architecturally closer to PC software than PlayStation releases, which shortens the path to a workable port, and AI programming tools have sped up the decompilation work that such conversions require.
It also extends a turbulent launch window for Grand Theft Auto 6. Crypto traders have repeatedly tried to profit from the game's release, including one who captured about $66,000 amid confusion over ticker symbols. The title's digital-only, disc-free format has separately drawn criticism, with GameStop's chief executive arguing that all-digital games have hurt consumers.
The leak has arrived alongside a wave of fraudulent downloads. Security firm Kaspersky has logged 27,416 detections of GTA 6-related malware and unwanted software since June, according to ZDNET, with fake PC versions ranging from crude AI-generated clones to files designed to hijack machines for crypto mining or to steal personal data. The only official release remains the PlayStation 5 edition; PC players can currently stream it through Sony's Remote Play app.
Rockstar's habit of staggering platforms is central to the frustration driving interest in the leak. Red Dead Redemption 2 reached PC about a year after consoles, and Grand Theft Auto 5 took nearly two years.
For the industry, the stakes go beyond one title. If major new releases can be played free on other platforms within days of launch, publishers lose revenue that funds subsequent development - a threat that falls hardest on smaller studios. The likely defensive response would be tighter always-online requirements, which tend to inconvenience paying customers most.

CyberLeek has reportedly uploaded more than 200 GB of GTA VI XBOX game files online, but there is still one important file missing from the release: the main executable.
The files first appeared online on November 19, shortly after GTA VI’s launch. The package reportedly contains a large portion of the game’s Xbox development files, but without the executable, users cannot properly access or run the game.
According to Rockstar Games community researcher Lucas7yoshi , the uploaded files are indeed from an XBOX build of GTA VI. However, he pointed out that this is an older version of the game, as it does not even include the separate censorship version for Australia and New Zealand.
More importantly, the game’s assets are encrypted with a key obtained from the main executable. This means that simply downloading the files is not enough to access their contents.
CyberLeek initially announced that the missing executable would be released on November 23, regardless of whether its cryptocurrency reached a certain market value.

One of CyberLeek’s biggest claims is that the community could get the XBOX build running on PC within a week, potentially achieving performance above 30 FPS. However, this is far from guaranteed.
The uploaded files are from an XBOX version of GTA VI, not a native PC build. Even if the missing executable becomes available, getting the game running on PC would require additional work from developers and the emulation community.

articles.t: GTA 6: PC gamers welcome unofficial PC port despite potential damage to the industry
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 is finally here, but PC gamers are still waiting – at least for an official release. An unofficial PC version could already be on the way. Despite the potential damage such recompilations could do to the gaming industry, the prospect has been met with largely positive reactions online.
articles.txt:
On the day GTA 6 launched, hacker Cyberleek released large portions of the Xbox version , potentially paving the way for an unofficial PC port. The process in question is known as recompilation, which involves adapting a game's code to run on another platform. Cyberleek believes modders could get the game running on PC within a week. On Reddit , the otherwise controversial hacker is receiving plenty of support – despite the potential harm such releases could cause to game developers.
PC gamers are clearly frustrated about having to wait for GTA 6 . However, the enthusiasm surrounding the prospect of an unofficial PC version arriving so soon appears to be driven largely by resentment toward Rockstar's long-standing strategy of releasing its games on consoles first and PC later. Many users accuse Rockstar of deliberately encouraging players to buy the same game twice. Those eager to play GTA 6 at launch may purchase the console version, only to buy it again on PC later to enjoy improved graphics. Some commenters have even openly stated that they intend to play the unofficial port. Others hope that rapid progress on the recompilation will put pressure on Rockstar to bring forward the official PC release.
Whether the unofficial port will actually be playable next week remains uncertain. Modders are still missing a crucial file: the game's executable (EXE), without which it cannot be launched. Cyberleek says he plans to release it on November 23, but whether that will be enough to produce a working PC version so quickly remains to be seen. There are also broader concerns about the potential consequences of such recompilations. If newly released games become available for free on other platforms shortly after launch, developers could lose valuable revenue. For smaller studios in particular, those losses could threaten their survival. Over time, this could make it harder to finance new games and encourage publishers to introduce stricter always-online requirements – ultimately leaving players worse off as well.

articles.t: GTA 6 Quietly Mocks an Infamous Donald Trump Florida Moment
articles.chapeau: Rockstar said it wouldn't directly satirize Trump — but GTA 6 takes a shot anyway
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 takes place in Rockstar Games' fictional version of Florida, so many wondered how the game might tackle President Donald Trump, who spends much of his time at his private club, Mar-a-Lago. Prior to release, Rockstar dispelled any notion that the game might directly address the current President of the United States. Doing so might make the game feel dated, according to Rockstar North studio head Rob Nelson. Now that the game is out, fans have discovered that GTA 6 does quietly acknowledge Trump.
The Easter egg probably isn't what you're expecting, and it doesn't really mention the Republican President's controversial politics. The shout-out does, however, poke fun at Trump's infamy for allegedly skipping out on the bill. You may have already seen it without realizing what it is. The story is a hyper-localized one involving a 2023 Trump visit to Miami's iconic Cuban restaurant, Versailles.
According to the Miami New Times , Trump came to the restaurant after being arraigned at a Miami courthouse over allegations of retaining government secrets and conspiring to obstruct justice. When he arrived at the restaurant, there was a crowd — and they were so ecstatic to see him that they began singing "Happy Birthday" to him. His birthday was technically the next day, and the man had just been indicted on 37 federal charges , but it didn't matter. The fans evidently wanted to express their love for the politician/reality TV show host in some way.
Trump gladly lapped up the attention and responded by declaring there would be "food for everyone!" The crowd cheered: They thought Trump was implying he was going to pick up their tab.
You're never going to believe this , but Trump did not, in fact, purchase anything for anyone. The Miami New Times reported that the President only stuck around for about 10 minutes before leaving. Since the incident, there's been some debate over whether Trump truly slighted anyone during the visit . He wasn't there for long, so could anyone truly have expected him to pull out his wallet?
However you interpret it, GTA 6 hides a reference to this controversial Florida moment through a small detail in its digital recreation of Versailles. The video game version of the establishment is called Antoinette, but the restaurant's reputation as a Miami staple and the building's matching exteriors heavily imply that Antoinette is based on a real-world restaurant. Even the restaurant's proprietors have made this connection.
TikToker Quique took a closer look at the GTA 6 version of the locale and found that there's a flier hanging from one of the windows. It reads: "All government officials must pay before leaving. Thank you." The connection between the real-life incident and GTA 6 's joke seems clear, according to fans from Florida in the TikTok video's comments.
Image: Quique/Tiktok It's a funny reference that reflects Rockstar's dedication to capturing Florida , and Miami in particular, to the fullest possible extent. As far as things go, though, it's a fairly tame Donald Trump moment that won't ruffle many political feathers. For a series known for lampooning American politics, that's kind of disappointing. You can't really extricate Trump from Florida, after all.
Anyway, my favorite part of the whole story is the interviews the Miami New Times conducted with the people who serenaded Trump​​​​​​​ at the restaurant after the President left the premises.
"He's the only one that will fight for us, for you, for me, for the people watching this at home," he said of the encounter, in which the president had arguably failed to keep his promise to the public just minutes earlier.

articles.chapeau: Cyberleak affirme partager en torrent une build Xbox complète de Grand Theft Auto VI et prétend que les joueurs PC pourraient l'émuler en une semaine, mais aucun émulateur Xbox Series X|S fonctionnel n'existe.
articles.txt:

Cyberleak a déclaré dans un message du 19 novembre détenir la build Xbox complète et que les fichiers étaient diffusés immédiatement en torrent. Le calendrier d'une semaine est l'affirmation de Cyberleak elle-même, et elle mérite du scepticisme pour deux raisons. D'abord, le groupe a un historique documenté d'utilisation de fuites précédentes de GTA 6 pour faire monter un programme de cryptomonnaie de 250 000 dollars, donc ses dates annoncées sont mieux traitées comme des affirmations que comme des événements programmés.
Ensuite, et plus fondamentalement, l'émulation est peut-être le mauvais mot pour ce qui suivrait la sortie d'un exécutable. Aucun émulateur Xbox Series X|S fonctionnel n'existe encore, il n'y a donc pas de route toute prête d'une build Xbox extraite vers une version PC jouable. Un portage non officiel fonctionnel dépendrait plutôt d'une recompilation, convertissant le code de la console pour tourner nativement sur PC, un chemin bien plus lent et moins certain que les taux d'images par seconde dont se targue Cyberleak.
GTA 6 est sorti sur console le 19 novembre, et Rockstar n'a annoncé aucune version PC. Des rumeurs évoquent un portage officiel début 2027, et l'ancien directeur technique de Rockstar, Obbe Vermeij, a soutenu que le studio bénéficierait à sortir un portage PC tôt, compte tenu de l'essor des portages assistés par IA. Cyberleak, dont le nom apparaît sous la forme « Cyberleek » dans certains titres repris par la presse, indique que si la version Xbox ne débouche pas sur un portage PC, il se tournerait plutôt vers une version PS5.
Rockstar n'a fait aucune déclaration sur la fuite. Cyberleak affirme que l'exécutable Xbox suivra le 23 novembre, quel que soit le résultat du programme de cryptomonnaie.

Leaker Cyberleek says it holds a full Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI and is already leaking it by torrent, a dump that could hand PC players the game before Rockstar Games has even announced one for the platform.

GTA 6 : un pirate diffuse 209 Go du jeu, mais injouable sur PC
GTA 6 sur PC : 209 Go de fichiers auraient fuité, mais Cyberleek garde le seul élément qui permettrait de lancer le jeu
articles.chapeau: Le jour de la sortie de GTA 6 sur console, un build Xbox de 209 Go surgit en torrent et affole les joueurs PC. Derrière Cyberleek, memecoin et exécutable manquant brouillent les pistes et pourraient réserver de mauvaises surprises.
articles.txt:
Le jour de la sortie de GTA 6 sur console, un build Xbox de 209 Go surgit en torrent et affole les joueurs PC. Derrière Cyberleek, memecoin et exécutable manquant brouillent les pistes et pourraient réserver de mauvaises surprises.
209 Go de fichiers estampillés GTA 6 circulent déjà sur les réseaux de piratage, et la rumeur d’un port PC anticipé affole les joueurs. Derrière ce gigantesque torrent présenté comme un build Xbox de Grand Theft Auto VI , beaucoup imaginent déjà un crack miracle pour lancer le jeu sur Windows.
En réalité, l’archive est incomplète : le seul composant qui permettrait de démarrer GTA 6 est absent, et ce détail change tout. Derrière cette fuite attribuée au leaker Cyberleek , on retrouve aussi un montage autour d’un memecoin et un compte à rebours qui entretiennent la confusion, tandis que la requête « gta 6 209 go fuite xbox » explose déjà sur Google.
Selon plusieurs sites spécialisés, dont GTAViFrance et The GTA 6 Map, le torrent diffuse un prétendu build de développement intitulé « XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026) » pesant environ 209 Go. Il aurait été mis en ligne le 19 novembre 2026, jour de la sortie officielle de GTA 6 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S.
Les captures d’écran de l’arborescence montrent surtout des assets : textures, modèles 3D, scripts, fichiers audio et vidéos. En revanche, l’exécutable principal, le binaire qui lance le jeu sur Xbox, est absent. Sans lui, ces 209 Go restent injouables, aussi bien sur console que sur PC.
Aucune rédaction majeure n’a pu vérifier publiquement que ce build est complet ou authentique, et Rockstar Games comme Take Two restent silencieux. Pour l’instant, il s’agit d’une fuite probable d’assets, potentiellement exploitable pour du datamining ou des spoilers, mais pas d’une version de GTA 6 jouable sur PC .
Sur son site, Cyberleek affirme détenir l’exécutable manquant et lie sa diffusion à la capitalisation de son jeton crypto. Après un premier objectif de 30 M$ (environ 28 M€) en octobre, jamais atteint, le seuil a été abaissé à 15 M$ (environ 14 M€) pour débloquer le fameux fichier. Un compte à rebours de quelques jours affiche qu’une fois expiré, l’exécutable serait publié sur les sites de piratage, quel que soit le résultat.
Même dans ce scénario, parler de « GTA 6 PC » est trompeur. Il s’agit d’un build Xbox, compilé pour l’OS et les API de la Xbox Series X|S. L’architecture matérielle est proche d’un PC, mais aucun émulateur Xbox Series X fonctionnel ne permet aujourd’hui de faire tourner un jeu aussi lourd. Notebookcheck cite d’ailleurs la promesse suivante de Cyberleek : « Cyberleek believes hackers will find a way to emulate the console version for Windows within a week. »
En pratique, adapter ce build impliquerait soit une émulation encore inexistante à ce niveau, soit un long travail de décompilation et de réécriture, à haut risque juridique. Pour les joueurs PC, cette fuite ne crée donc aucune version jouable à court terme.
Le volet financier de l’affaire est tout aussi inquiétant. En octobre, Cyberleek avait déjà lié une précédente promesse de build jouable à un objectif de 30 M$ de capitalisation pour son token, opération qualifiée de rug pull après un crash brutal et au moins 250 000 $ (environ 230 000 €) de frais prélevés selon OnPoint 4 Gamers. D’où les mises en garde de nombreux sites qui déconseillent tout investissement.
Parallèlement, des torrents et faux installateurs « GTA 6 PC » se multiplient. Kaspersky signale déjà des dizaines de milliers de téléchargements infectés liés à GTA 6. Derrière un fichier de 209 Go présenté comme un crack miracle peuvent se cacher ransomwares, voleurs de mots de passe ou mineurs de crypto.
En France, télécharger illégalement GTA 6 reste de toute façon risqué juridiquement, avec une surveillance renforcée de l’ARCOM. Concrètement, pour un joueur PC français, cette fuite ne change rien : GTA 6 n’existe officiellement que sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, aucune date PC n’a été annoncée, et ces 209 Go sans exécutable n’apportent ni version jouable ni avantage, seulement des dangers techniques et financiers.

Les fuites continuent tant qu’un meme coin à son nom, le $CYBERLEEK, prend de la valeur. Début octobre, il avait frappé fort avec une vidéo de 25 minutes où l’on voyait Jason et Lucia entièrement nus, y compris en cinématique . Il y faisait même apparaître un tank de nulle part, ce qui montrait clairement qu’il avait accès au menu debug d’une build jouable.
L’objectif à l’époque était une capitalisation de 30 millions de dollars . Entre temps, la cryptomonnaie s’est effondrée et Cyberleek a disparu à la mi-octobre avec un message d’adieu en trois parties. Rockstar et Take-Two n’ont visiblement jamais réussi à mettre la main sur lui.
Le jour de la sortie du jeu, son site a publié un nouveau message. Cyberleek y affirme diffuser par torrent une build Xbox complète de GTA 6 datée de novembre 2026, qui pèse environ 209 Go , donc grosso modo la taille du jeu sur console. Il manque cependant un fichier, et pas des moindres : l’exécutable principal, sans lequel rien ne se lance.
Ce fichier ne sortira que si le $CYBERLEEK atteint 15 millions de dollars de capitalisation, ou le 23 novembre quoi qu’il arrive. Le leaker assure aussi que la communauté arrivera à émuler cette version Xbox en moins d’une semaine, à plus de 30 fps. Si ça ne marche pas, il promet de s’attaquer à une build PS5.
Il faut quand même garder du recul, puisque l’émulation d’un jeu Xbox Series sur PC n’a rien d’une simple formalité , donc la promesse d’une version PC piratée en une semaine relève surtout du marketing de crypto.
Si vous êtes tenté de jeter un œil, sachez que ce genre de fuite attire les escrocs. Des chercheurs ont déjà repéré de faux installeurs « GTA 6 PC » qui servaient en réalité à installer des infostealers, ces logiciels qui récupèrent vos mots de passe . Un exécutable trouvé sur un forum quelques jours après une fuite non vérifiée, c’est exactement ce qu’il faut éviter. Le $CYBERLEEK s’est déjà effondré une fois, donc acheter cette crypto revient surtout à financer le prochain chantage.

articles.txt:
Le groupe de hackers Cyberleek assure avoir mis en ligne une build de développement de GTA 6 pour Xbox datée de novembre 2026, mais retient volontairement le fichier exécutable principal tant que son jeton crypto n'atteint pas une valeur fixée.
Crédit : Rockstar Games Le groupe Cyberleek a refait surface, affirmant avoir publié une véritable build de développement de Grand Theft Auto VI . La dernière mise à jour de son site affiche un lien intitulé « XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026) » , et des captures d'écran circulant sur les réseaux sociaux semblent montrer des fichiers issus d'une build de développement de la version Xbox du jeu.
Problème pour quiconque voudrait la lancer : le fichier exécutable principal manque à l'appel, ce qui rend la build totalement injouable en l'état. Un tweet de Jose Coixao ( @notnotzecoxao ), daté du 19 novembre 2026, évoque une taille totale de 209 Go pour l'ensemble des fichiers.
L'annonce a été publiée sur le site du groupe le 19 novembre. Cyberleek affirme retenir l'exécutable sur un compte à rebours, mais promet de le publier plus tôt si son jeton crypto atteint une certaine valeur de marché. Un chiffre précis circule : le groupe ne lâcherait l'exécutable que si la capitalisation du meme coin $CYBERLEEK atteint 15 millions de dollars.
Cyberleek insiste sur un point : il s'agit bien d'une build pensée pour Xbox, et non d'une version PC. Le groupe assure même que la communauté parviendra à l'émuler en une semaine, en dépassant les 30 images par seconde.
Le groupe situe cette fuite dans une campagne plus large contre Rockstar, qu'il présente comme une défense des droits des consommateurs. Il reproche notamment au studio de sortir GTA 6 uniquement en version numérique, et avait déjà diffusé des mois durant des clips de gameplay présentés comme authentiques, y compris avant la révélation officielle du jeu par Rockstar via Netflix. Le calendrier exact de ce retour reste flou : certaines informations évoquent le premier retour du groupe depuis le lancement de GTA 6, d'autres un compte resté actif en pleine semaine de sortie. L'authenticité des fichiers n'est pas confirmée non plus : les captures « semblent » montrer une vraie build de développement, sans vérification possible des fichiers eux-mêmes.
Ce n'est pas la première fois que Cyberleek joue cette carte. En octobre déjà, le groupe avait menacé de publier une build de GTA 6, conditionnant cette fois le déblocage à un jeton atteignant 30 millions de dollars. Le groupe avait alors publié une série de fuites de plus en plus poussées, incluant des images dénudées de Lucia, l'une des deux personnages jouables. Mais le jeton s'était effondré après coup, et le compte avait de nouveau disparu.
Cyberleek encourage depuis longtemps les dons en cryptomonnaie, et les a même rendus obligatoires pour participer aux votes qui déterminent la prochaine fuite. Le groupe aurait déjà encaissé ses gains sur ce meme coin une première fois. On ignore toujours si la personne à l'origine des vidéos diffusées tout l'été est la même que celle qui a relancé le compte aujourd'hui, ou si plusieurs personnes sont impliquées.
Du côté de Take-Two, la traque continue. L'éditeur affirme que ses efforts pour retrouver le fuiteur évoluent rapidement (« rapidly evolving »), et a déposé plusieurs assignations auprès de Discord pour obtenir des informations sur des serveurs et utilisateurs précis. Malgré ça, Rockstar Games et Take-Two n'ont toujours pas réussi à identifier les personnes derrière le compte.

articles.chapeau: Le groupe CyberLeek affirme diffuser par torrent une build Xbox de GTA 6. L'exécutable manque, promis contre la hausse de sa cryptomonnaie.
articles.txt:
Le jour même de la sortie de Grand Theft Auto VI , le groupe CyberLeek a refait surface. Une mise à jour publiée sur son site le 19 novembre renvoie vers un fichier intitulé « XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026) ». Le groupe affirme détenir la version complète du jeu de Rockstar Games , compilée en novembre 2026 pour Xbox Series X|S , et la distribuer par torrent. « C'est fait. Elle est diffusée par torrent. Maintenant » , annonce le message, relayé par Kotaku et Video Games Chronicle .
L'archive pèse 209 Go, un volume signalé sur les réseaux sociaux par Jose Coixao le soir même ( ndlr : son compte X n'existe plus à l'heure actuelle ). Il y manque un seul fichier, l'exécutable principal, sans lequel rien ne peut se lancer. CyberLeek le retient derrière un compte à rebours : « À zéro, l'exécutable est publié, sans condition » . Le groupe promet de le libérer plus tôt si son jeton $CYBERLEEK atteint une capitalisation de 15 millions de dollars. Le seuil était fixé à 30 millions en octobre, avant que le cours ne s'effondre. « C'était trop ambitieux. La moitié semble juste » , justifie désormais le site. Le groupe avait alors multiplié les fuites, jusqu'à des images dénudées de Lucia, l'une des deux héroïnes jouables.
Ni Kotaku ni VGC n'ont pu vérifier le contenu de l'archive. Les captures qui circulent semblent montrer les fichiers d'une build de développement, sans plus. Rockstar et Take-Two n'ont pas réagi à cette nouvelle fuite. L'éditeur a déjà lancé plusieurs assignations visant Discord pour identifier les membres du groupe, sans résultat visible à ce jour.
La promesse vise d'abord les joueurs PC, puisque le jeu n'est sorti que sur PS5 et Xbox Series . Le site l'assume sans détour : « C'est une version Xbox cette fois, pas une version PC. CL s'en moque. Cette communauté l'aura émulée en moins d'une semaine, bien au-delà de 30 images par seconde » . Il évoque aussi une build PS5 en solution de repli si la version Xbox ne donne rien, une option « probablement jamais nécessaire » . Aucune démonstration n'appuie ces affirmations. Une build Xbox ne se lance pas telle quelle sous Windows : il faut comprendre et contourner l'environnement de la console, et aucun émulateur Xbox Series fonctionnel n'existe aujourd'hui. Côté PlayStation, la scène s'active autour d' un premier dump de GTA 6 sur PS5 , mais l'émulation de la console reste balbutiante.
Le choix d'une version Xbox plutôt que PS5 intrigue, et le délai annoncé laisse sceptique. Dans la scène, l'idée qui domine est qu'un GTA VI jouable sur PC prendra des années plutôt que des jours, pour un jeu réputé plafonner à 30 images par seconde sur consoles. Les quelques jeux Xbox récents qui tournent sur PC, comme les Forza , le doivent à leur propre version Windows, pas à un émulateur.
CyberLeek se présente en défenseur des consommateurs. Il reproche à Rockstar une sortie sans disque, dont l'édition physique se limite à un code de téléchargement . Son message lance « pas de double paiement pour Take-Two et Rockstar » et rappelle avoir conseillé de ne pas précommander : « Voici l'une des raisons » . Depuis des mois, le groupe publie des extraits de gameplay authentiques. Il réserve aussi le vote dans ses sondages aux auteurs de dons en cryptomonnaie, et, selon Kotaku , il a déjà encaissé une partie des gains de son jeton.
Le groupe ne s'en cache pas. Dans un message intitulé « The End of the Road », publié en octobre et toujours visible sur son site, il reconnaît : « CL a vendu deux fois » . La première vente aurait déclenché une cascade, les autres détenteurs revendant à leur tour, et le groupe s'est vu reprocher l'effondrement du cours. Sa défense tient en deux phrases : « Le jeton a toujours été un don, jamais un investissement. Aucun rendement promis, ni sous-entendu » . Les accusations, elles, viendraient de « gens qui n'ont jamais ouvert la blockchain. Surtout des YouTubeurs » . Tant que rien n'est vérifié, la prudence s'impose : n'acheter aucun jeton, ne connecter aucun portefeuille de cryptomonnaies et ne lancer aucun exécutable d'origine inconnue.
